jane_acme_corp: Hey team — noticed lots of 503s and spikes to ~800ms for completions this morning. Example request_id=req_20240304_9f7b2. Happening across different endpoints. Starting around 08:12 UTC.

maya_support: Thanks for the report, Jane. Sorry about that. Can you paste one curl repro we can run (with a redacted API key) and the request_id you mentioned? Also, did anything change on your side (model pin, auth keys, billing)?

jane_acme_corp: Curl below (key redacted). No config changes on our side, we do pin to `redwood-model-2` but have a canary rollout enabled via our feature flag.

jane_acme_corp: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-model-2","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":128}'
```

jane_acme_corp: request_id=req_20240304_9f7b2, sample response headers: `x-request-id: req_20240304_9f7b2`, `x-server-latency-ms: 812`, body was 503 with `{"error":"service_unavailable"}`

maya_support: Got it — I'm opening a debug bundle request. @sara_eng_oncall can you check whether any canary pods for `redwood-model-2` were scaled/rolled today? Also whether fallback routing kicked in.

sara_eng_oncall: Looking now. I see a brief canary push at 07:58 UTC and an automated rollback at 08:10 UTC for that model (DeployBot event below). Logs show increased cache misses and a surge in KV-store timeouts.

deploybot: [08:10 UTC] rollback: rollout redwood-model-2-canary -> stable due to SLO violation (error_rate > 5%).

sara_eng_oncall: Can you generate a debug bundle for the failing request? Maya — I need the raw headers (auth method), and if possible the `x-client-ts` from the request. If billing was involved (rate limit/overage) it could cause 401/402 path but not 503.

maya_support: Jane — can you confirm billing status? BillingBot shows a recent declined card event on your org; sometimes that triggers rate-limiting/soft-block paths. If billing is an issue we can whitelist to reproduce.

billingbot: [automated] acme-corp: payment source last_transaction_status=declined (code: card_expired) at 2024-03-03T22:45:11Z. No hard block in place; usage continues but alerting escalated.

jane_acme_corp: Oh, we had a billing hiccup but team fixed the card at 08:05 UTC. Shouldn't be blocked now.

maya_support: Okay. To help repro we need: 1) exact curl you ran (you provided), 2) the request_id (provided), 3) the raw response body + headers (you gave partial), 4) debug bundle: please run `POST /v1/debug-bundles` with `x-request-id` attached. Here's a quick curl to create an uploadable debug bundle on our side:

maya_support: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/debug-bundles \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"request_ids":["req_20240304_9f7b2"],"notes":"Customer repro - high latency and 503s, possible canary rollback"}'
```

jane_acme_corp: Bundle created: https://debug.redwood.example/bundles/DBG-7854 (uploaded).

sara_eng_oncall: Thanks — pulled the bundle. Key excerpts: backend shard reported `KV_TIMEOUT` spikes, and one canary instance returned `503` with stack: 

sara_eng_oncall: ```
[2024-03-04T08:09:57Z] model-worker-7 | ERROR ServeLoop failed to fetch kv for prefix 0x3a7d - timeout after 600ms
[2024-03-04T08:10:01Z] model-worker-7 | WARN Falling back to nearest-variant redwood-model-1 (compat)
[2024-03-04T08:10:02Z] model-worker-2 | INFO Response status=200 latency_ms=142
```

sara_eng_oncall: That lines up — a hotspot in KV reads caused the canary to fail and traffic to fallback to older variant; however some in-flight requests hit the failing instance and returned 503.

maya_support: For immediate mitigation you can pin to stable variant explicitly to avoid canary traffic until infra is fully remediated. Ping me when done and I'll run a synthetic load to confirm.

jane_acme_corp: How do we pin programmatically? Our infra uses the API.

sara_eng_oncall: Two options: 1) At your side, set `model: \"redwood-model-2@stable\"` in the generate call (explicit version tag). 2) We can force route your org to stable on our side until the canary is healthy — if you want us to, reply with `please_force_pin`.

jane_acme_corp: I'll try (1) now.

jane_acme_corp: Update: switched to `redwood-model-2@stable` in curl, reran. Response returned 200 with latency ~135ms for the same prompt, request_id=req_20240304_9f7b2-2.

maya_support: Great. Can you keep an eye on it for the next 30m and report any regressions? We'll follow up with a postmortem.

sara_eng_oncall: Following up on infra — KV timeouts were due to a degraded redis cluster causing increased tail latencies. We spun replacement nodes and cleared backlog at 08:28 UTC. Canary rollout will be retried once tail latencies are stable.

deploybot: [08:28 UTC] cluster_event: redis-cluster autoscale -> +2 nodes; health ok.

maya_support: Closing loop: cause = KV-store tail latency spike -> canary pod failures -> in-flight hits to failing canary returned 503. Mitigation = pin to stable variant or wait until canary completes retry after infra recovery. Action items: Infra to monitor KV tail; SRE to add autoscaling trigger at 95th-percentile latency; Support to notify customer when canary is reattempted.

jane_acme_corp: Thanks all — pin worked. Please confirm when canary is safe to enable again. :thumbsup:
